analysis.title: JPM | US Special Situations Daily: November 06, 2026 (ROKU/FOX close deal, Unity Gains on Report Silver Lake and PIF Held Talks to Buy)
key_insights: Fox closed its acquisition of Roku. Roku holders receive $95.30 in cash plus 0.9799 FOX Class A shares per share. FOX holders own about 74% of the combined company and former Roku holders about 26%. Roku stops trading on Nasdaq on 11/6.
The closing terms differ slightly from the announced terms of $96.00 cash and 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per Roku share.

Reuters reported that Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's PIF approached Unity Software about a buyout at a valuation of about $25B. Silver Lake already owns roughly 8% of Unity, which has reportedly hired an investment bank to evaluate options. Unity shares rose on the report.

Varonis (VRNS) / Thoma Bravo: the preliminary proxy was filed. HSR expires 11/18, with foreign investment and antitrust approvals needed in Australia, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the UK. Closing guidance is H1 2027. The deal price is $49.75 per share.

Varonis proxy background: Proofpoint/Thoma Bravo bid $36.00 (5/17), $43.00 (8/11), $46.50 (8/13), $49.50 (8/17) and a 'best and final' $49.75 (8/18). Varonis countered at $54.00 (8/16) and $50.00 (8/18). Sponsor D's $38-40 offer on 8/5 was rejected. The board cited no competing proposal, no financing condition and AI disruption risk to a standalone path.

Brookfield Infrastructure received all approvals for its simplification, combining BIP and Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation. Closing is expected 11/19/2026, with securityholders receiving Class A shares of BIP Inc. one-for-one.
Devon Energy holders Toms and Kimmeridge are increasing pressure on the company to sell.

Brighthouse Financial 3Q26: JPM calls core earnings and business trends poor. Merger update and capital movement matter more for the stock. BHF and Aquarian are discussing extending the merger date beyond December 2026, and JPM thinks Aquarian is in a strong position to renegotiate a lower price. BLIC statutory capital was backfilled by a $600M extraordinary dividend from BRCD.

Rhythm Pharmaceuticals: Reuters and WSJ reported AstraZeneca made a ~$10B offer at a ~$124-134 per share range including milestone payments. JPM (Priyanka Grover) says the range does not reflect the company's value and models $4.0B peak sales in 2037, which supports a value in the $140s per share. Rhythm is an AFL Top Pick.

Rail merger (UP/NS): JPM's D.C. conversations point to roughly a 50/50 chance of STB approval, in line with market-implied odds. The STB raised concerns that UP CEO Jim Vena's remarks may have discouraged stakeholders from speaking freely. Kloster is seen as a possible swing vote. Full asks are due 11/18 and DOJ/USDOT preliminary comments are due 12/3.

JPM says the UP/NS merger puts a heavy burden on the applicants to prove no competitive harm from combining two largely end-to-end networks, and that the deal could face more scrutiny next year under a Democratic Congress.

PTC 4QF26: constant-currency ARR growth excluding divestitures accelerated to 9.7% from 9.1%, above the 9%-9.5% guidance range. Revenue was $673M, down 25% y/y. FY26 free cash flow was about $873M, up 2% y/y. Guidance is suspended pending the Schneider Electric acquisition, which is expected to close in H1 2027. JPM keeps Neutral and a $205 target.

Desk flows: ADT and OGN were two-way with arb demand and arb supply. LNTH is a good two-way call. The desk was better to buy SLN and VRNS, better to sell CART, QGEN, BRZE, CZR and MGM, and better to set RXO/CHRW and ROKU/FOXA.
Event-driven options activity: TSLA had 111 trades over 500 contracts, GFL 13, WEN 8, MAT 3 and BILL 2.
Risk arb calendar for 11/6: the EC Phase I review for Akzo Nobel/Axalta expires, and Utz reports with no call.

market_movers.rationale: JPM calls Rhythm an AFL Top Pick. The reported AstraZeneca offer range of ~$124-134 per share undervalues the company. JPM's peak sales model of $4.0B in 2037 supports the $140s per share.
ARR growth accelerated to 9.7% and free cash flow beat guidance. Guidance is suspended pending the Schneider Electric acquisition.
Reuters reported Silver Lake and PIF approached Unity about a buyout valuing it at about $25B. Silver Lake already holds roughly 8%.
JPM calls the quarter weak and sees Aquarian in a strong position to renegotiate the merger to a lower price.
The Thoma Bravo deal at $49.75 per share awaits HSR (expires 11/18) and foreign approvals. The desk was better to buy VRNS.

earnings_insights: PTC 4QF26 (reported): revenue $673M, down 25% y/y (24% constant currency), within the $630M-$690M guidance range and above its midpoint. 4Q free cash flow was about $38M against about $15M guidance. FY26 free cash flow was about $873M against a prior outlook of about $850M.
Brighthouse Financial 3Q26 (reported): JPM calls core earnings poor. The BLIC statutory capital was backfilled by a $600M extraordinary dividend from BRCD.
Rhythm: JPM models peak sales of $4.0B worldwide in 2037, including $2.3B in acquired hypothalamic obesity in 2036 and $1.4B in Prader-Willi syndrome in 2037 (JPM estimates, not reported).

trade_ideas.rationale: Reflects the desk's read of the day's merger-arb flows.

risk_factors: UP/NS merger may fail STB approval, with the odds put at roughly 50/50. DOJ and USDOT comments are due 12/3.
BHF/Aquarian merger date may be extended past December 2026 at a lower price.
Varonis deal needs HSR and approvals in five foreign jurisdictions.
The Rhythm offer is only reported and not confirmed.

Arb flow: the desk saw arb demand and arb supply in ADT (over ~5M shares traded) and OGN, and LO supply with arb demand in LNTH.

tension_points.bull_case: The merger could be approved with conditions, as the STB approved UP-SP and CP-KCS despite DOJ objections. Kloster is seen as a possible swing vote.
tension_points.bear_case: UP's strategy of treating the application as a negotiation is questioned. The STB raised concerns about retaliation, and Kloster said the applicants 'still have a long way to go'. DOJ could challenge the competitive-harm view.
tension_points.what_invalidates: DOJ and USDOT preliminary comments due December 3, and the November 18 filing of full asks, are the next tests of the approval odds.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees value in the $140s per share on peak sales of $4.0B in 2037.
tension_points.bear_case: The reported AstraZeneca range of ~$124-134 per share may be what a buyer is willing to pay, and the offer is only reported.
